record.original_question: Find good heuristics to compute candidates for question 1.6.15.5.

evidence.quote: Find good heuristics to compute candidates for question 1.6.15.5.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A finite word u over an alphabet A is called an abelian cube if it can be written as a concatenation u = u_1 u_2 u_3 of three nonempty factors that are pairwise permutations of each other (equivalently, the three factors have the same Parikh vector). An infinite word w avoids long abelian cubes if there exists an integer N such that w contains no abelian cube of length at least N as a factor.

Setup. Fix the four-letter alphabet B = {0, 1, 3, 4} and a morphism h : B* → B* admitting an infinite fixed point h^∞(0) starting with 0 (so that h(0) begins with 0 and |h^n(0)| → ∞). Consider morphisms g : B* → {0,1}* and the associated infinite binary word g(h^∞(0)).

Underlying open question. Decide whether there exists a morphism g : B* → {0,1}* such that the binary infinite word g(h^∞(0)) avoids long abelian cubes.

Problem. Devise effective heuristics for generating, ranking, and pruning candidate morphisms g : {0,1,3,4}* → {0,1}* that are plausible solutions to the above question. Concretely, design and justify computable criteria — for instance, bounds on the lengths |g(a)| for a ∈ B, structural conditions on the images g(a), parity or Parikh-balance conditions, prefix/suffix constraints inherited from h, and finite-window abelian-cube tests on truncations of g(h^∞(0)) — that can be combined into a search procedure which, for prescribed image-length budgets, enumerates only a tractable family of candidates g while provably eliminating those that quickly produce arbitrarily long abelian cubes in g(h^∞(0)).
artifact.status_search_result: The question is part of a list of open problems collected from the WORDS conferences and is phrased as a meta-question seeking heuristics to attack a related open question on avoidance of long abelian cubes by morphic binary words. No publication settling the heuristic question itself was located. Related work (e.g., Currie–Rampersad–Mol–Shallit on additive/abelian k-powers, Rao–Rosenfeld on long k-abelian repetitions) develops template/parent-based search techniques but does not claim to resolve this specific heuristic question.

status_evidence.title: Extending Dekking's construction of an infinite binary word avoiding abelian cubes
status_evidence.snippet: Studies binary morphic words avoiding additive/abelian cubes via template-based search.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on related avoidance questions does not resolve the heuristic problem.
